warning: These are historical interpretations, not current adjudications. Source status and similarity arguments must be re-evaluated against the current reasons.
description: ACTL8 is a divergent, testis-enriched member of the actin family whose molecular function has not been determined. The 366-residue protein retains the actin fold but is only about a third identical to cytoplasmic beta-actin, and structural comparison shows the divergence is concentrated exactly where actin's identity resides: most of the ATP phosphate- and adenosine-binding residues survive, whereas the great majority of the protomer-protomer contact surface that builds a filament, including almost the whole DNase-I binding loop, does not, which makes canonical incorporation into a two-stranded filament unlikely. Whether it polymerises at all has never been tested, and no biochemical activity, ligand or cellular structure has been assigned to it experimentally. Expression is strongest in testis and pancreas with weak placental expression, and the protein is detected by proteomics and by immunohistochemistry in the cytoplasm of tumour cells. ACTL8 is also known as cancer/testis antigen 57, and this accounts for essentially all of its functional literature: it is transcriptionally silent in most somatic tissues but reactivated in breast, gastric, oral squamous, lung and head-and-neck carcinomas, and in several of these high expression has been associated with poor survival. In that ectopic setting, RNA-interference knockdown reproducibly reduces proliferation, migration and invasion, increases apoptosis, slows cell-cycle progression and lowers PI3K/AKT/mTOR phosphorylation, and shRNA knockdown suppresses xenograft growth; no direct interaction with any pathway component has been demonstrated, so the route is unresolved and may be indirect. Its physiological role in the testis, the one tissue where it is normally abundant, remains unstudied. The only reported binding partner is the ceramide transfer protein CERT1, from yeast two-hybrid screening alone.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic inference that ACTL8 acts in the actin cytoskeleton, from the deepest of the three PANTHER nodes cited anywhere in this gene's GOA record. This row is treated differently from the other ten IBA rows, and the reason is the clade the donating node covers rather than the quality of its donors.
PTN002631484 donates GO:0015629 to eighteen human genes, spanning the conventional actins (ACTA1, ACTA2, ACTB, ACTC1, ACTG1, ACTG2), the POTE actin-fusion genes, and the divergent actin-like proteins ACTL8, ACTL9, ACTL10, ACTRT1, ACTRT2 and ACTRT3 - identity to beta-actin across that set runs from 33.7 to 100 per cent. That is a node whose reconstructed ancestral state genuinely is the shared actin-fold state, and the term it donates is correspondingly generic: "The part of the cytoskeleton (the internal framework of a cell) composed of actin and associated proteins. Includes actin cytoskeleton-associated complexes." So the breadth of this term is not a granularity failure - it is the true last common ancestor of a heterogeneous donor set, and no specificity upgrade is warranted. Of the 25 WITH/FROM tokens on this row, 24 resolve to protein entries and 23 of those carry their own IDA for the term, spanning 12 organisms; the exception is pig ACTB (Q6QAQ1), which carries IPI.
A comparison across ACTL8's own relatives closes the argument. Of the eight divergent human actin-like and actin-related-T proteins, ACTL8 is the only one that receives an IBA from either narrow node: ACTL7A and ACTL7B draw on PTN001377938, PTN008986520 and PTN008986528, while ACTL9, ACTL10, ACTRT1, ACTRT2 and ACTRT3 all draw on PTN000940351 and this same deep node PTN002631484. The consequence is quantitative - ACTL8 carries 11 IBA rows against a median of 2 across its seven relatives, a roughly five-fold inflation traceable to one tree placement.
It is retained as non-core rather than accepted because no direct evidence places ACTL8 in this compartment. UniProt's own subcellular location for ACTL8 is Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton with evidence code ECO:0000250 - by similarity, and with no source entry cited - so the only non-phylogenetic support for cytoskeletal residence is itself a similarity statement.
review.reason: Correctly scoped family-level inference, and the only IBA row on this gene whose donating node spans the divergent actin-like proteins rather than the near-identical cytoplasmic actins. It is kept because it asserts nothing that the sequence contradicts, and marked non-core because no experiment has localised ACTL8 to the actin cytoskeleton and because a generic compartment term cannot represent the core of a gene whose activity is unknown.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of beta- and gamma-actin's synaptic localisation. The donors are sound and heavily characterised - human ACTB carries EXP plus IDA x 5 plus IMP x 2 for this term, mouse Actb IDA x 6, mouse Actg1 IDA x 6, rat Actg1 IDA x 4 - so nothing here is wrong at source. The problem is the transfer.
The donating node PTN007551913 has exactly nine human descendants: ACTB, ACTG1, ACTBL2, POTEE, POTEF, POTEI, POTEJ, POTEKP and ACTL8. Eight of the nine are at least 90.7 per cent identical to beta-actin over their aligned actin block - each POTE protein carries a C-terminal actin-family domain, per its UniProt SIMILARITY line, which is what places them here. ACTL8 is the ninth, at 33.8 per cent. Unlike the deep node behind GO:0015629, this donor set is not heterogeneous - it is a beta-actin subfamily, so its reconstructed ancestral state is beta-actin's cell biology in all but name, and transferring that to a protein 57 percentage points less similar than any other member is not a family-level inference.
Nothing independent supports a synaptic pool of ACTL8. Expression is strongest in testis and pancreas, HPA classifies the gene as tissue-enriched in testis, and the only protein-level localisation reported anywhere is moderate focal cytoplasmic staining in head-and-neck carcinoma. Presence at a synapse is a claim about a cell type for which ACTL8 has no reported expression or localisation - and as on the axon row, that is absence of positive evidence rather than demonstrated absence, since HPA tissue-enrichment does not imply zero neuronal transcript and one of UniProt's cDNA clones came from brain.
review.reason: A cell-type-specific compartment inherited from near-identical cytoplasmic actins by a node that mis-places ACTL8. Two independent reasons: the donating clade is a beta-actin subfamily into which ACTL8 falls at 33.8 per cent identity while every other member exceeds 90 per cent, and the structural basis for a synaptic actin pool - incorporation into filaments - is the property ACTL8 has lost, with only 11 of 38 protomer-interface positions chemically compatible and 8 of 10 D-loop contacts non-conservatively substituted - a score that puts ACTL8 in a band with the other divergent actin-likes and above human Arp3, so it argues that canonical protomer incorporation is unlikely rather than that filament association is impossible. Removing this row does not require deciding what ACTL8 does; it requires only that it is not beta-actin, and that no evidence places it at a synapse.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of cytoplasmic residence. This is the one row from the narrow beta-actin node that survives, because it happens to be independently verifiable in human tissue rather than only inferable from the tree.
Immunohistochemistry on head-and-neck squamous carcinoma with an anti-ACTL8 antibody shows moderate focal cytoplasmic staining, described by the authors as confirming expression at the protein level. ACTL8 also has no signal peptide, no transmembrane segment and no organelle-targeting feature in its UniProt feature table, and it is recorded at PE 1 from proteomics. Cytoplasmic is therefore the compartment statement the human data actually supports, and it is the level at which ACTL8's localisation should currently be recorded.
It is a generic term and so cannot be core, and the is_active_in relation is stronger than the evidence - the protein is present in the cytoplasm, but no activity has been localised anywhere. A curator revisiting this row should consider whether located_in is the better relation, and whether the immunohistochemistry in PMID:41129177 supports upgrading the evidence code.
review.reason: Correct and, unusually for this gene, corroborated outside the phylogeny: anti-ACTL8 immunohistochemistry on human tumour tissue gives cytoplasmic staining, and the protein carries no targeting signal that would put it elsewhere. Kept rather than marked over-annotated because nothing about it is inflated - it is the least specific and best-supported statement in the record. Non-core rather than accepted-as-core for internal consistency: core_functions is deliberately empty because no molecular function is established, so no row on this gene can be asserted as core, and a bare cytoplasm term could not carry that weight even if one could. The open question is the relation, not the term.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of a membrane association from beta-actin. In conventional actin this annotation reflects the cortical network beneath the plasma membrane - actin is not an integral membrane protein, it is a polymer that a membrane is attached to. The term's definition is explicitly about a bilayer: "A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it."
Two things make this a poor transfer. ACTL8's UniProt feature table contains no transmembrane segment, no signal peptide, no lipidation site and no membrane-binding region - the whole table is one CHAIN and two dbSNP variants. And the mechanism by which an actin becomes membrane-attached, cortical filament formation, is the capability ACTL8 has no support for: only 11 of 38 protomer-interface positions are chemically compatible with beta-actin, which in the panel ranking places it among the divergent actin-likes rather than uniquely low (human Arp3 scores 8), so this weighs against a cortical network without settling it.
Marked over-annotated rather than removed because "membrane" is broad enough that a peripheral, indirect association cannot be excluded for any cytoplasmic protein, and because GO already treats bare membrane annotations as low-information. Nothing positive supports it.
review.reason: Uninformative compartment term whose only basis is beta-actin's cortical pool, transferred by the node that mis-places ACTL8. ACTL8 has no membrane-targeting feature of any kind, and the route by which an actin reaches a membrane - polymerisation into a cortical network - is precisely the property its interface substitutions argue against. Not removed because a peripheral association is unfalsifiable at this term's granularity; flagged so that it is not read as evidence of membrane residence.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of beta- and gamma-actin's axonal pool, from the same node that produces the synapse row. Mouse Actb and Actg1 each carry IDA x 3 plus IMP for axon and rat Actb carries IDA, so the source annotations are solid; the transfer is the failure.
Axonal localisation is a claim about a neuronal compartment. ACTL8 is testis-enriched in HPA, strongly expressed in testis and pancreas per UniProt, and has no reported neuronal expression or localisation. HPA tissue-enrichment does not imply zero neuronal transcript - one of UniProt's cDNA clones was in fact isolated from brain - so the point is the absence of any positive evidence for an axonal pool, not a demonstrated absence of the protein. Its only reported protein-level localisation is cytoplasmic staining in carcinoma tissue. As with synapse, the residual mechanism that would put an actin into an axonal cytoskeleton is filament incorporation, which the interface analysis argues against - though only at the strength that canonical protomer incorporation is unlikely, since human Arp3 scores below ACTL8 on the same metric while occupying a protomer position at an Arp2/3 branch. The decisive point for this row is the absence of any neuronal evidence, not the tally.
review.reason: Neuronal compartment inherited from near-identical cytoplasmic actins through a node in which ACTL8 is the sole divergent member. No expression, imaging or proteomic evidence places ACTL8 in a neuron, and the structural basis for the transferred property is absent. This is the same failure as the synapse and axonogenesis rows and should be corrected together with them.

term.label: structural constituent of postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton

review.summary:
This is the only molecular function ACTL8 carries other than bare protein binding, and it is the row where the propagation failure is most direct, because the term names the exact property the sequence has lost. Its definition is "The action of a molecule that contributes to the structural integrity of a postsynaptic actin cytoskeleton" - a structural contribution to an actin network, in a postsynaptic compartment.
Structural contribution to an actin network means being part of the polymer. Computing the F-actin protomer-protomer interface directly from PDB 6DJO gives 38 residues within 4.0 angstrom of a neighbouring protomer; of these ACTL8 retains 8 identical and 3 conservatively substituted and has 24 non-conservative substitutions plus 3 deletions, so only 11 of 38 positions are chemically compatible. Within the DNase-I binding loop, which makes the principal longitudinal contact and is anchored in the alignment by an invariant proline, 8 of 10 contacts are non-conservative: R39 to C38, Q41 to E40, G42 to N41, V43 to P42, M44 to G43, V45 to P44, M47 to Y46, Q49 to R48. Beta-actin scores 37 identical plus 1 conservative on the same set, and Drosophila Arp53D - a genuinely divergent actin-like protein that does polymerise - scores 29 plus 4. Both tallies are unchanged under a second substitution matrix and gap model.
The metric has to be read at its real strength, and the analysis itself supplies the limit. Ranked over the whole panel, ACTL8's 11 of 38 sits in a band with the other divergent actin-likes - ACTL7A 14, ACTL7B and ACTL9 16, ACTRT1 21 - and **human Arp3 (ACTR3) scores 8, below ACTL8**, with Arp2 at 22. Arp2 and Arp3 form the first protomer pair of a daughter filament at an Arp2/3 branch, so they demonstrably do occupy protomer positions in an actin-containing structure. A low score therefore bounds *canonical incorporation into a conventional two-stranded filament*; it does not establish that a protein cannot be part of any actin-containing assembly. Stated at that strength the structural half of this row shows the transferred structural role is unsupported rather than impossible - which is why the REMOVE rests on the postsynaptic half, below, and not on the tally alone.
The postsynaptic half fails independently: the donors are human ACTB (EXP plus IDA x 3 plus IMP) and rat Actg1 (IDA x 2), and there is no evidence ACTL8 is present in a neuron at all. The donating node PTN002631586 contains only ACTB, ACTG1, ACTBL2, the five POTE genes and ACTL8, with ACTL8 the sole member below 90 per cent identity to beta-actin.
review.reason: The transferred molecular function is a structural contribution to an actin polymer in a postsynaptic compartment, and both halves are contradicted for ACTL8 by independent evidence. Structurally, only 11 of 38 filament-interface positions are compatible with beta-actin and 8 of 10 D-loop contacts are non-conservatively substituted, so canonical protomer incorporation is unlikely and there is no positive basis for ACTL8 contributing structural integrity to an actin network - stated at that strength because human Arp3 scores lower still on the same metric while occupying a protomer position at an Arp2/3 branch. Contextually, ACTL8 is testis-enriched with no reported neuronal expression or synaptic localisation, while the donors' evidence is entirely from conventional actin in neurons. The donating node is a beta-actin subfamily in which ACTL8 is the only divergent member. This is a positive argument for removal rather than a hedge: the annotation asserts a specific physical property that the sequence lacks.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of residence in an actin filament, from the same narrow node as GO:0098973. The term's definition is specific about what a filament is: "A filamentous structure formed of a two-stranded helical polymer of the protein actin and associated proteins."
The interface analysis argues against ACTL8 forming such a polymer: 24 of 38 protomer-contact positions are non-conservatively substituted, 3 fall in a deletion, and the D-loop is almost entirely rewritten. Nothing in the human data places ACTL8 on a filament either.
The tally does not settle the row on its own, and the reason is visible in the same analysis: ranked across the panel, ACTL8's 11 of 38 lies in a band with ACTL7A (14), ACTL7B and ACTL9 (16) and ACTRT1 (21), and human Arp3 (ACTR3) scores 8 - lower than ACTL8 - while Arp2 scores 22. Both Arps occupy protomer positions at an Arp2/3 branch, so the metric bounds canonical two-stranded protomer incorporation rather than filament association in general. That is exactly why this row is hedged rather than removed.
This row is marked over-annotated rather than removed, and the difference from GO:0098973 is deliberate. GO:0098973 makes two extra claims - that ACTL8 performs a structural function, and that it does so postsynaptically - and both are separately contradicted. GO:0005884 says only that ACTL8 is active in an actin filament, and the definition's phrase "and associated proteins" leaves room for a non-polymerising protein to be present in the structure, for instance by capping or by sub-stoichiometric incorporation into a heteropolymer. That has not been tested, so it is unsupported rather than refuted.
review.reason: Unsupported rather than demonstrably wrong. The residues that would let ACTL8 polymerise are largely gone, so it should not be presented as a filament component, but the term admits associated proteins as well as protomers and no experiment has asked whether ACTL8 binds or decorates F-actin. Deliberately weaker than the REMOVE on GO:0098973, which additionally asserts a structural role and a postsynaptic location. The polymerisation question is listed under suggested_experiments; a pyrene-actin or cosedimentation result would settle this row either way.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of a neuronal developmental process, resting on two sources: the mis-placing node PTN007551913 and rat Actb, which carries its own IDA for axonogenesis. This is the thinnest support of any IBA row on the gene - a single protein donor.
Axon outgrowth depends on regulated actin polymerisation in the growth cone. Assigning ACTL8 to it requires both that ACTL8 be present in developing neurons and that it participate in actin dynamics there; neither is supported. ACTL8 is testis-enriched, has no reported neuronal expression, and has lost most of the polymerisation interface.
review.reason: Neuronal developmental process inherited from beta-actin with a single protein donor, no expression evidence in neurons, and no structural basis for participating in actin dynamics. It is also downstream of the same node error as the axon and synapse rows, so it should be corrected with them rather than separately. GO_REF:0000033 rows like this one are exactly the case where an over-propagated electronic inference can be argued against on biological grounds.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of a binding term whose donors carry it by IPI rather than IDA - human ACTB has IBA plus IPI, rat Actb IBA plus IPI plus ISO. So the source evidence is interaction-detection, and the term itself ("Binding to a protein kinase, any enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group, usually from ATP, to a protein substrate") names an entire enzyme class rather than a partner.
Conventional actin does associate with many kinases, but which kinase, and in what context, is what carries the biology; the parent term records none of it. There is no evidence that ACTL8 binds any kinase. Its only reported partner is CERT1, from yeast two-hybrid, which is not a protein kinase. Repository curation guidance discourages exactly this kind of uninformative binding annotation.
review.reason: Promiscuous, uninformative binding term transferred by the node that mis-places ACTL8, with no gene-specific support and no named partner. Marked over-annotated rather than removed because the donors' own evidence is real interaction data and because a protein of this fold binding some kinase somewhere is not falsifiable at this granularity - which is itself the objection. If a specific kinase is ever identified, the annotation should be replaced by an informative term with the partner recorded, not by this parent.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of membership in a specific multiprotein complex, from human ACTB (IDA x 2) via the node that mis-places ACTL8. This is the clearest error in the record, because the GO term's own definition names which actin belongs to the complex.
GO:0035267 is defined as "A complex having histone acetylase activity on chromatin, as well as ATPase, DNA helicase and structural DNA binding activities... Subunits of the human complex include HTATIP/TIP60, TRRAP, RUVBL1, BUVBL2, beta-actin and BAF53/ACTL6A." The actin content of the human NuA4/TIP60 complex is therefore specified at the level of individual paralogs: beta-actin and the actin-related protein ACTL6A. Complex membership is a property of particular subunits, established by purification of that subunit, and it does not propagate down a family by sequence similarity - yet this node assigns it to gamma-actin, ACTBL2, ACTL8 and the five POTE proteins as well. The definition says the subunits "include" beta-actin and BAF53/ACTL6A rather than "only", so it does not by itself exclude another actin paralog; what it does show is that the complex's actin content is recorded per paralog, from purification, and no purification places ACTL8 there.
No purification, immunoprecipitation or proteomic study places ACTL8 in NuA4/TIP60 or in any other complex. ACTL8 is also a cytoplasmic, testis-enriched protein with no reported nuclear pool.
review.reason: Complex membership does not transfer by family similarity, and here the term's own definition settles it by naming beta-actin and ACTL6A as the complex's actin subunits. The annotation was generated by a node that assigns NuA4 membership to all nine of its human descendants. ACTB's row is the one that should stand: it has its own IDA and the term's definition names it. Of the remaining eight, ACTL8, ACTBL2 and the five POTE genes have no supporting purification at all, and ACTG1 is the borderline case - the definition says the human subunits "include" beta-actin and BAF53/ACTL6A rather than "only", so it does not exclude gamma-actin, but nor does anything place it there. There is no purification or proteomic evidence for ACTL8 in any complex, and no evidence of a nuclear pool.

review.summary:
Phylogenetic transfer of involvement in cell motility from human ACTB (IBA plus IMP) via the mis-placing node. Unlike the other rows from that node, this one has a genuine human counterpart in the literature - but it points at a different term.
The IBA reflects actin's role as the motility machinery itself: GO:0048870 is defined as "Any process involved in the controlled self-propelled movement of a cell that results in translocation of the cell from one place to another", and conventional actin is involved in it by being the polymer that generates the protrusion. ACTL8, with 24 of 38 protomer-contact positions non-conservatively substituted, has no demonstrated place in that machinery.
What the human data show is regulation, and it belongs on a separate row rather than as a replacement term here. RNA-interference knockdown of ACTL8 reduces migration and invasion in triple-negative breast cancer cells, gastric cancer cells, oral squamous carcinoma cells and lung adenocarcinoma cells, across four independent laboratories, with shRNA knockdown also suppressing xenograft growth. No experiment shows ACTL8 in the cytoskeletal machinery; the phenotype is loss of a positive input into migration.
This row was initially marked MODIFY with GO:0030335 as a replacement. That was wrong on mechanics. MODIFY changes the term but leaves the evidence code and reference untouched, so the replacement would still be an IBA on GO_REF:0000033 with PTN007551913 in WITH/FROM - which amounts to asking PAINT to reconstruct positive regulation of cell migration as the ancestral state at the very node this review argues mis-places ACTL8. It is not a supportable ancestral call either: beta-actin's own evidence for GO:0048870 is that it *is* the motility machinery, not that it regulates migration. So the IBA is removed on the same grounds as its sibling rows from that node, and the human RNAi evidence is recorded as a separate NEW row for GO:0030335 with evidence_type IMP - the same shape already used for GO:0008284, built from the same four papers.
review.reason: Transferred from the node that mis-places ACTL8, and the term asserts membership of the motility machinery itself - GO:0048870 covers "the controlled self-propelled movement of a cell", which conventional actin is involved in by being the polymer that generates the protrusion. ACTL8 has no demonstrated place in that machinery. Removed rather than modified because MODIFY would retain IBA/GO_REF:0000033 from PTN007551913 and merely swap the term, leaving an ancestral-state claim that beta-actin's own IMP does not support. The human evidence that ACTL8 influences migration is real and is preserved on a separate NEW GO:0030335 IMP row, where the evidence code matches the experiments.

review.summary:
Automatic mapping from UniProt's subcellular-location vocabulary. The WITH/FROM token UniProtKB-SubCell:SL-0090 is a controlled-vocabulary identifier rather than another gene's evidence, so unlike the IBA rows there is no donor protein to interrogate; the source is a UniProt annotation statement.
Tracing it back gives the reason to flag this row. The statement it derives from is "SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton {ECO:0000250}" - ECO:0000250 is sequence-similarity evidence, and no source entry is cited after the code, so the similarity is untraceable. The chain is therefore: an uncited by-similarity curator statement becomes a controlled-vocabulary term, which becomes an IEA annotation that reads as independent of the IBA rows. It is not independent; it is a second rendering of the same family-level inference.
The term itself has to be kept, and the reason is ontological rather than evidential. GO:0015629 actin cytoskeleton is a descendant of GO:0005856 cytoskeleton, so retaining the child while calling the parent an over-annotation would assert that ACTL8 is in the actin cytoskeleton but that saying "cytoskeleton" overshoots - which cannot both hold. This row was initially marked MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED; that was inconsistent with keeping GO:0015629. The criticism it was carrying is a redundancy and provenance complaint, not an over-annotation, and that is recorded here and in the root_cause instead.
review.reason: Kept because GO:0015629, which this review retains, is a descendant of GO:0005856, so the two rows must move together and cannot be given opposite verdicts. Non-core because it is the most generic possible localisation statement. What is wrong with it is not the term but its provenance: it re-encodes a UniProt ECO:0000250 subcellular-location statement that cites no source entry, so it adds no evidence and must not be counted as a second, independently-coded line of support for cytoskeletal residence. The uncited ECO:0000250 is worth reporting to UniProt, which is recorded in suggested_questions.

supported_by.supporting_text: CC   -!- SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Cytoplasm, cytoskeleton {ECO:0000250}.

The UniProt statement behind it is ECO:0000250 by similarity with no source entry cited, which makes this annotation a re-encoding of the same family-level inference that the IBA rows already express.

review.summary:
Automatic inter-ontology inference: the WITH/FROM field is the GO id GO:0098973, so this biological process was generated from ACTL8's molecular-function annotation rather than from any evidence about ACTL8. There is no source gene and no source publication.
Since the GO:0098973 row is itself an IBA that this review removes, this row is a propagation from a propagation and falls with its parent. Its content compounds both problems of the parent - it asserts participation in organising a postsynaptic actin network, which requires both the polymerisation capability the interface analysis argues against and a neuronal localisation for which there is no evidence.
review.reason: Derived automatically from GO:0098973, which this review removes; with its only input gone there is nothing left to support it. It also inherits both independent objections to the parent - the loss of most of the F-actin protomer interface and the absence of any neuronal expression or localisation evidence for a testis-enriched protein. This row is a mechanical consequence and should be retracted in the same GOA update as GO:0098973 rather than argued separately.
